papers.title: Selective Cooperative Perception via Blind Spot Reasoning and Agentic Dialogue with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Real-time cooperative perception (CP) in multi-agent traffic environments is highly resource-intensive, which posing scalability challenges for large-scale deployment. Efficiency can be significantly improved by selectively performing CP only in safety-critical scenarios and for key occluding objects. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are well-suited for complex reasoning in dynamic and uncertain environments, making them a promising tool for this selective CP task. This study proposes a VLM-driven agentic framework for blind spot reasoning and dialogue-based CP. A mixed-model architecture is designed that integrates conventional object detection for stable perception, vision-language reasoning for identifying impactful occlusions, and a physics-based geometric module to align reasoning with real-world visibility constraints. The framework also incorporates a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting mechanism to enhance interpretability and intent-aware decision-making. We collect real-world data from connected vehicles operating in urban traffic and compare the driving-critical blind spot identification and dialogue performance of four state-of-the-art VLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves over 80% accuracy in driving-critical blind spot detection and over 90% success in dialogue-driven perception sharing. This work provides a scalable, interpretable, and bandwidth-efficient alternative to conventional CP pipelines, and offers new insights into agentic communication design for future connected traffic systems.
papers.abstract_zh: 多智能体交通环境中的实时协同感知（CP）资源消耗巨大，给大规模部署带来可扩展性挑战。仅在安全关键场景和关键遮挡对象上选择性地执行CP，可显著提升效率。视觉语言模型（VLM）擅长在动态和不确定环境中进行复杂推理，因而成为这一选择性CP任务的有前景工具。本研究提出一种由VLM驱动的智能体框架，用于盲区推理和基于对话的CP。设计了一种混合模型架构，将用于稳定感知的传统目标检测、用于识别有影响遮挡的视觉语言推理，以及用于使推理与真实可见性约束对齐的基于物理的几何模块相集成。该框架还引入思维链（CoT）提示机制，以增强可解释性和意图感知决策。我们采集了在城市交通中运行的网联车辆的真实数据，并比较了四种最先进VLM在驾驶关键盲区识别和对话方面的性能。实验结果表明，我们的方法在驾驶关键盲区检测上达到超过80%的准确率，在对话驱动的感知共享上达到超过90%的成功率。这项工作为传统CP流水线提供了一种可扩展、可解释且带宽高效的替代方案，并为未来网联交通系统的智能体通信设计提供了新见解。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出VLM驱动的智能体框架，结合目标检测、视觉语言推理与几何模块进行盲区推理和对话式协同感知，在真实网联车辆数据上实现超80%的驾驶关键盲区检测准确率和超90%的对话感知共享成功率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DISCOVER: Online Variance-Guided Data Discovery for Budgeted Multimodal GRPO
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in reinforcement learning have made verifiable rewards a central post-training paradigm for improving multimodal reasoning. However, methods such as GRPO remain data- and compute-inefficient, spending rollout and annotation budget on prompts that provide little learning signal. We propose DISCOVER, an online data-discovery framework for budgeted multimodal GRPO that enables vision-language models to dynamically identify prompts that are most useful for the current policy. DISCOVER first organizes the multimodal sample pool into semantic clusters and queries a small set of density-diverse representative samples to obtain initial reward observations. During training, it estimates the utility of unannotated samples by transferring sparse reward feedback from queried samples. Since sample utility changes as the policy evolves, DISCOVER dynamically updates these estimates with recency-weighted rollout observations. It then selects only high-utility prompts for annotation using a policy-conditioned score that accounts for reward variance and difficulty. Once the discovery budget is exhausted, DISCOVER continues with utility-based replay. Experiments on ViRL39K and VLAA-Thinking with Qwen3-VL-2B show that DISCOVER substantially improves multimodal mathematical reasoning under a strict 10% unique-sample budget, outperforming budget-matched random selection, hard-example sampling, full-pool GRPO under the same training-step budget, and online selection baselines. Ablations further validate the importance of semantic coverage, online reward transfer, and stable discovery cadence, establishing DISCOVER as a practical framework for data-efficient multimodal RL post-training.
papers.abstract_zh: 强化学习的最新进展使可验证奖励成为改进多模态推理的核心后训练范式。然而，GRPO等方法仍存在数据和计算效率低的问题，将 rollout 和标注预算花费在提供很少学习信号的提示上。我们提出DISCOVER，一种面向预算受限多模态GRPO的在线数据发现框架，使视觉语言模型能够动态识别对当前策略最有用的提示。DISCOVER首先将多模态样本池组织为语义簇，并查询一小组密度多样的代表性样本以获得初始奖励观测。在训练过程中，它通过迁移来自已查询样本的稀疏奖励反馈来估计未标注样本的效用。由于样本效用随策略演化而变化，DISCOVER利用近期加权 rollout 观测动态更新这些估计。随后，它使用考虑奖励方差和难度的策略条件分数，仅选择高效用提示进行标注。一旦发现预算耗尽，DISCOVER继续基于效用的回放。在ViRL39K和VLAA-Thinking上使用Qwen3-VL-2B的实验表明，在严格的10%唯一样本预算下，DISCOVER显著提升了多模态数学推理，优于预算匹配的随机选择、困难样本采样、相同训练步数预算下的全池GRPO以及在线选择基线。消融实验进一步验证了语义覆盖、在线奖励迁移和稳定发现节奏的重要性，确立了DISCOVER作为数据高效多模态RL后训练的实用框架。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出DISCOVER在线数据发现框架，通过语义聚类、奖励迁移和策略条件选择在10%样本预算下为多模态GRPO挑选高效用提示，在ViRL39K和VLAA-Thinking上显著提升多模态数学推理。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Large Language Models as a Universal Searcher for Open-World Automated Machine Learning
papers.abstract_en: Developing effective machine learning models requires complex manual tuning, while current Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) frameworks remain domain-specific and isolate model architecture, training hyperparameter, and data ratio optimization. Here, we bridge this gap by proposing a universal, large language model (LLM)-based AutoML framework that jointly optimizes these configurations for the first time without the need for task-specific fine-tuning. We propose NCode, a unified numerical encoding scheme that translates diverse AutoML design choices into universal discrete sequences and effectively reframes the optimization process as a unified ranking task. Trained solely on optimization trajectories derived from a limited, single-domain vision task, the proposed LLM-based searcher demonstrates impressive cross-task, cross-modality and joint search-space optimization generalizability, achieving state-of-the-art performance across image classification, image segmentation, speaker verification and text-to-image benchmarks. Crucially, it exhibits superior scalability in the large-scale training and joint optimization of a billion-parameter Diffusion Transformer, requiring 896 GPU-days and attaining a state-of-the-art GenEval score of 0.91. By leveraging reinforcement learning to instill Chain-of-Thought reasoning, we provide a systematic way to interpret the LLM-based searcher's internal decision-making mechanisms, revealing its optimization strategy shifted from the early-stage diversity-driven exploration to the late-stage anchor exploitation. Our proposed framework provides a scalable, generalizable, and interpretable pathway toward general-purpose open-world machine learning optimization.
papers.abstract_zh: 开发有效的机器学习模型需要复杂的人工调优，而当前的自动化机器学习（AutoML）框架仍局限于特定领域，并将模型架构、训练超参数和数据比例优化相互隔离。在此，我们通过提出一个通用的、基于大语言模型（LLM）的AutoML框架来弥合这一差距，该框架首次联合优化这些配置，且无需任务特定微调。我们提出NCode，一种统一的数值编码方案，将多样的AutoML设计选择转化为通用离散序列，并有效地将优化过程重构为统一排序任务。所提出的基于LLM的搜索器仅在一个有限单领域视觉任务的优化轨迹上训练，却展现出令人印象深刻的跨任务、跨模态和联合搜索空间优化泛化能力，在图像分类、图像分割、说话人验证和文本到图像基准上取得最先进性能。关键的是，它在十亿参数扩散Transformer的大规模训练和联合优化中展现出优越的可扩展性，需要896 GPU天并达到0.91的最先进GenEval分数。通过利用强化学习灌输思维链推理，我们提供了一种系统化方式来解释基于LLM的搜索器的内部决策机制，揭示其优化策略从早期多样性驱动的探索转向后期锚点利用。我们提出的框架为通用开放世界机器学习优化提供了一条可扩展、可泛化且可解释的路径。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于LLM的通用AutoML框架NCode，将架构、超参数与数据比例选择统一编码为排序任务，仅用单领域视觉轨迹训练即实现跨任务跨模态泛化，并在十亿参数扩散Transformer联合优化中达到0.91 GenEval分数。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, transformer
匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pre-training
papers.abstract_en: Medical Vision-Language Pre-training (VLP) leverages the semantic richness of radiology reports to learn 3D representations, yet current architectures remain fundamentally anatomy-agnostic. While clinical diagnostics rely on organ-specific context, standard encoders apply a uniform, dense parameterization to all volumetric patches, and existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routers gate on isolated local features without explicit access to the organ composition of the scan or crop. We propose Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts (A$^{2}$MoE), a framework that incorporates anatomical inductive biases within the model's computational path. A$^{2}$MoE introduces two key components: (1) a Histogram Representation Router (HRR) that conditions expert selection on global visual context and a predicted anatomical composition histogram, encouraging anatomy-dependent expert weighting; and (2) an Organ-Query Multi-Scale Projector (OQMSP) that utilizes learnable queries to extract organ-level embeddings for fine-grained alignment without requiring manual annotations at inference. By routing at the patch level rather than the token level, A$^{2}$MoE reduces routing complexity by orders of magnitude while satisfying load balancing by construction. Pre-trained on over 60,000 multi-phase CT scans, A$^{2}$MoE achieves state-of-the-art performance across segmentation, classification, and detection benchmarks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our anatomically grounded inductive biases support robust generalization to MRI and ultrasound, establishing a scalable foundation for medical representation learning. The code is available at https://github.com/gmum/A2MoE.
papers.abstract_zh: 医学视觉语言预训练（VLP）利用放射学报告的语义丰富性来学习3D表示，但当前架构从根本上仍与解剖结构无关。尽管临床诊断依赖器官特定上下文，标准编码器对所有体积块施加统一的稠密参数化，而现有专家混合（MoE）路由器仅基于孤立的局部特征进行门控，无法显式访问扫描或裁剪区域的器官组成。我们提出解剖激活专家混合（A$^{2}$MoE），一种在模型计算路径中引入解剖归纳偏置的框架。A$^{2}$MoE引入两个关键组件：（1）直方图表示路由器（HRR），其专家选择以全局视觉上下文和预测的解剖组成直方图为条件，鼓励依赖解剖结构的专家加权；（2）器官查询多尺度投影器（OQMSP），利用可学习查询提取器官级嵌入以进行细粒度对齐，且推理时无需人工标注。通过在块级而非 token 级进行路由，A$^{2}$MoE将路由复杂度降低数个数量级，同时通过构造满足负载均衡。在超过60,000次多期CT扫描上预训练后，A$^{2}$MoE在分割、分类和检测基准上取得最先进性能。此外，我们证明解剖学基础的归纳偏置支持对MRI和超声的稳健泛化，为医学表示学习建立了可扩展基础。代码见 https://github.com/gmum/A2MoE。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出A$^{2}$MoE框架，通过直方图表示路由器和器官查询多尺度投影器在块级引入解剖归纳偏置，在6万余次多期CT上预训练后在分割、分类、检测基准上达到最先进，并泛化至MRI和超声。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training
evidence: 开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting
papers.abstract_en: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity. Existing robust preference optimization methods primarily operate at the sequence level, implicitly treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. However, rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps, while preferred responses can include subtle errors. In this work, we propose \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization via \textbf{R}obust \textbf{T}oken-level reweighting \textbf{(PORT)}, a fine-grained framework for robust alignment under noisy preferences. PORT performs token-level reweighting using the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) of token log-probabilities, yielding an efficient forward-pass-only proxy to gradient-norm penalization that selectively suppresses corrupted tokens without additional backward-pass computation. We provide theoretical analysis showing that PORT reduces the gradient bias from noisy preference labels by minimizing an upper bound on the bias term. Extensive experiments across diverse noise settings demonstrate that PORT consistently improves robustness and outperforms existing sequence-level baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT
papers.abstract_zh: 偏好优化已成为使大语言模型与人类价值对齐的核心方法，但其有效性在很大程度上取决于偏好标注的质量。在实践中，由于标注错误和歧义，偏好数据往往带有噪声。现有的鲁棒偏好优化方法主要在序列级操作，隐含地将整个回复视为统一正确或错误。然而，被拒绝的回复仍可能包含有信息量的推理步骤，而被偏好的回复也可能包含细微错误。在本工作中，我们提出通过鲁棒 token 级重加权进行偏好优化（PORT），一种在噪声偏好下进行鲁棒对齐的细粒度框架。PORT利用 token 对数概率的经验累积分布函数（CDF）进行 token 级重加权，产生一种仅需前向传播的高效梯度范数惩罚代理，在不增加反向传播计算的情况下选择性抑制损坏的 token。我们提供理论分析，表明PORT通过最小化偏差项的上界来减少噪声偏好标签带来的梯度偏差。跨多种噪声设置的广泛实验表明，PORT持续提升鲁棒性并优于现有序列级基线。代码见 https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出PORT框架，利用token对数概率的经验CDF进行token级重加权，以仅前向传播的方式选择性抑制噪声偏好中的损坏token，理论证明其降低梯度偏差并在多种噪声设置下优于序列级基线。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：preference optimization
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment, theoretical analysis
开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models have emerged as promising paradigms for decoding brain activity through large-scale self-supervised pretraining. Notably, most existing approaches employ masked patch reconstruction, in which randomly selected EEG patches are masked and recovered by the network. However, purely random masking may limit representation learning as informative patches from highly correlated channels often remain unmasked, causing the network to underutilize weakly correlated channels or serial dependencies. Furthermore, because these models are typically based on transformer architectures, their performance is influenced by the choice of positional encoding. Although positional encoding has been extensively explored in natural language processing and computer vision, few studies have adapted it to the unique characteristics of EEG signals. To address these limitations, this study introduces a conditional positional encoding method based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to explicitly model inter-channel correlations, along with an adaptive masking strategy that enhances representation learning by modulating the difficulty of masked patch reconstruction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to integrate graph-based representations into conditional positional encoding and introduce adaptive masking within EEG foundation model pretraining. Experimental results on ten benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed GCN-based positional encoding and adaptive masking strategies, both individually and in combination, achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance, highlighting their effectiveness in EEG foundation modeling.
papers.abstract_zh: 脑电图（EEG）基础模型已成为通过大规模自监督预训练解码大脑活动的一种有前景的范式。值得注意的是，大多数现有方法采用掩码图块重建，即随机选择EEG图块进行掩码并由网络恢复。然而，纯随机掩码可能限制表征学习，因为来自高度相关通道的信息性图块往往未被掩码，导致网络未能充分利用弱相关通道或序列依赖关系。此外，由于这些模型通常基于Transformer架构，其性能受位置编码选择的影响。尽管位置编码在自然语言处理和计算机视觉中已被广泛探索，但很少有研究将其适配于EEG信号的独特特性。为解决这些局限，本研究引入一种基于图卷积网络（GCN）的条件位置编码方法，以显式建模通道间相关性，并提出一种自适应掩码策略，通过调节掩码图块重建的难度来增强表征学习。据我们所知，这是首个将基于图的表示集成到条件位置编码中、并在EEG基础模型预训练中引入自适应掩码的研究。在十个基准数据集上的实验结果表明，所提出的基于GCN的位置编码与自适应掩码策略（单独及组合使用）均达到最先进或具有竞争力的性能，凸显了它们在EEG基础建模中的有效性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于GCN的条件位置编码与自适应掩码策略用于EEG基础模型预训练，在十个基准数据集上单独或组合使用均取得最先进或竞争性性能。

匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture

papers.title: TMT: Adapting CLIP to Infrared Imagery via Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models such as CLIP achieve strong performance across computer vision tasks, yet their image-text alignment is less reliable for infrared (IR) imagery because large-scale pre-training is dominated by visible-spectrum data. Due to the high cost of the infrared-text labeling, we investigate adapting CLIP to IR through only paired infrared-visible images, which requires considering modality-specific knowledge while preserving scene content and CLIP's image-text alignment. To achieve this, we propose TMT (Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer), which adapts CLIP's image encoder through a text-defined infrared-to-visible direction and supervision from paired IR-visible images. First, we found that modality discrepancy can be described by corresponding text embeddings, thus using the direction of text embedding differences to guide the knowledge transfer between visible and infrared modalities without erasing infrared-specific information. To enhance the representation of semantics and details of infrared images, we introduce Generative-Perceptual Co-Supervision that combines semantic alignment from CLIP visible image encoder with diffusion noise-prediction feedbacks. On four source-disjoint IR classification benchmarks, TMT achieves the highest mean zero-shot accuracy among the compared methods (48.92%). It also achieves the best IR-text retrieval results among the compared methods without infrared-text supervision during adaptation and the highest open-vocabulary segmentation mIoU on both CART and SemanticRT among the CLIP-like methods.
papers.abstract_zh: CLIP等视觉-语言模型在各类计算机视觉任务中表现强劲，但由于大规模预训练以可见光数据为主，其图像-文本对齐对红外（IR）图像不够可靠。鉴于红外-文本标注成本高昂，我们研究仅通过成对的红外-可见光图像将CLIP适配到红外模态，这需要在保留场景内容和CLIP图像-文本对齐的同时考虑模态特定知识。为此，我们提出TMT（文本导出的模态知识迁移），通过文本定义的红外到可见光方向以及成对红外-可见光图像的监督来适配CLIP的图像编码器。首先，我们发现模态差异可由对应的文本嵌入描述，因此利用文本嵌入差异的方向引导可见光与红外模态间的知识迁移，而不抹除红外特有信息。为增强红外图像语义与细节的表示，我们引入生成-感知协同监督，结合来自CLIP可见光图像编码器的语义对齐与扩散噪声预测反馈。在四个源不相交的红外分类基准上，TMT在对比方法中取得最高平均零样本准确率（48.92%）。在适配期间无红外-文本监督的情况下，它也在对比方法中取得最佳红外-文本检索结果，并在CLIP类方法中于CART和SemanticRT上取得最高开放词汇分割mIoU。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出TMT，利用文本嵌入差异方向与成对红外-可见光图像监督将CLIP适配到红外模态，在四个红外分类基准上取得48.92%的平均零样本准确率。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: What Broke & Why: Practical Lessons from Reinforcement Learning Post-Training
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important way to improve how language models reason, solve problems, and use tools. But getting it to work in practice is not always straightforward. Training can fail because a model receives no useful reward, learns to exploit the reward system, stops exploring, or appears to improve when the evaluation itself is misleading. In this book, we give a practical introduction to reinforcement learning post-training for language models, focusing on what works, what fails, and why. We begin with the foundations of post-training, explain GRPO and the training loop step by step, and then follow five training programs covering math reasoning, search agents, training stability, mixture-of-experts models, and software engineering tasks. Each program shows the problems encountered, the changes made, and the lessons learned. The book also examines what reinforcement learning actually changes inside a model. The remaining chapters provide a practical reference for reward design, evaluation, training tool-using agents, debugging common failures, reproducibility, rollout engines, and hardware. Written for researchers and practitioners working with open models, the book aims to help readers understand how to train models, recognize when something goes wrong, and decide what to try next.
papers.abstract_zh: 带可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）已成为提升语言模型推理、问题求解和工具使用能力的重要方式。但在实践中使其奏效并不总是简单直接。训练可能因模型得不到有用奖励、学会利用奖励系统、停止探索，或评估本身具有误导性而看似改进却实际失败。本书对语言模型的强化学习后训练进行实用介绍，聚焦于哪些做法有效、哪些失败及其原因。我们从后训练基础开始，逐步解释GRPO与训练循环，随后介绍五个训练项目，涵盖数学推理、搜索智能体、训练稳定性、混合专家模型和软件工程任务。每个项目展示所遇到的问题、所做的修改以及得到的经验教训。本书还考察强化学习究竟在模型内部改变了什么。其余章节为奖励设计、评估、训练工具使用智能体、调试常见失败、可复现性、rollout引擎和硬件提供实用参考。本书面向使用开放模型的研究者与实践者，旨在帮助读者理解如何训练模型、识别何时出现问题，并决定下一步尝试什么。
papers.tldr_zh: 本书以五个训练项目（数学推理、搜索智能体、训练稳定性、混合专家模型、软件工程）为例，系统总结语言模型强化学习后训练中有效与失败的做法及其原因。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery
papers.abstract_en: Vision language models (VLMs) encode substantial expert knowledge within their weights, yet their direct application to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery remains limited. Meanwhile, vision transformers trained on these tasks rely predominantly on low-level visual latents (colours, textures, and shapes) that lack the higher-level reasoning humans employ for identification. We propose Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label (GHiML) learning, a pipeline that extracts conceptual latent variables from a VLM conditioned on training data, generates sample-relevant captions grounded in those variables, and fuses the resulting textual embeddings with image embeddings via cross-attention and a per-node gated router. We also introduce the inverted HML score ($d_{\mathrm{inv}}$), a similarity score that evaluates hierarchical multi-label predictions through graph traversal distance and a cardinality penalty, providing an interpretable alternative to existing measures, which are insensitive to realistic degradations in sparse, deep hierarchies. Experiments on BenthicNet, FathomNet and iNaturalist show that the router improves macro $F_1$ over the vision-only baseline by up to 6.7 pp and $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ by up to 21.1 pp on in-domain benthic data, with gains persisting under distribution shift. Ablations locate the contribution of the text itself: on the multi-label biotic hierarchies, removing the per-sample text signal degrades $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ while leaving macro $F_1$ unchanged, consistent with text acting through prediction cardinality rather than node discrimination, whereas iNaturalist, whose annotations are single-label, loses 18.7% of macro $F_1$. Our results support the hypothesis that VLMs contain exploitable specialised knowledge that, when appropriately elicited, can augment classification in domains where direct visual learning is insufficient.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在其权重中编码了大量专家知识，但其在底栖图像等专业分类领域的直接应用仍然有限。与此同时，在这些任务上训练的视觉Transformer主要依赖低级视觉潜变量（颜色、纹理和形状），缺乏人类用于识别的高层推理。我们提出引导式层次多标签（GHiML）学习，这是一条流水线：以训练数据为条件从VLM中提取概念潜变量，生成基于这些变量的样本相关描述，并通过交叉注意力和逐节点门控路由器将所得文本嵌入与图像嵌入融合。我们还引入倒置HML分数（$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$），一种通过图遍历距离和基数惩罚评估层次多标签预测的相似度分数，为现有度量（对稀疏、深层层次结构中现实退化不敏感）提供可解释的替代方案。在BenthicNet、FathomNet和iNaturalist上的实验表明，该路由器在域内底栖数据上将宏$F_1$较纯视觉基线提升最多6.7个百分点，将$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$提升最多21.1个百分点，且在分布偏移下增益持续存在。消融实验定位了文本本身的贡献：在多标签生物层次结构上，移除逐样本文本信号会降低$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$而宏$F_1$不变，这与文本通过预测基数而非节点判别起作用的结论一致；而标注为单标签的iNaturalist则损失18.7%的宏$F_1$。我们的结果支持如下假设：VLM包含可被利用的专业知识，在适当引出后能够增强直接视觉学习不足领域的分类。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出GHiML，从VLM提取概念潜变量生成描述并与图像嵌入融合，在底栖数据上宏F1最高提升6.7个百分点，并引入倒置HML分数$d_{\mathrm{inv}}$。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
papers.abstract_en: While Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) accelerates isolated algorithm and kernel synthesis, distributed LLM training depends on tightly coupled launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules, where single edits often hit out-of-memory (OOM) boundaries, compiler conflicts, measurement jitter, or silent numerical drift. We present InfraRSI, the agentic harness that turns open-ended human commands into verified training optimizations via a five-stage workflow: init locks editable scope and a fixed task contract over workload, loss, and timing invariants to prevent reward hacking, doctor profiles baseline phases and calibrates cluster noise, run co-optimizes launch knobs and code patches before re-verifying top candidates against the baseline and logging findings to a cross-hardware experience bank, and report and apply audit source paths, track failed-trial costs, and commit promoted changes. Rather than stepping greedily from a single incumbent, InfraRSI initializes from diverse experience-seeded configurations and fits global execution-time and censored peak-memory models across all trials, including OOMs. Using these models, it prices per-setting memory costs, revises miscalibrated LLM priors from live runs, and pairs memory-hungry optimizations with memory savers and verified code patches. Across four single- and multi-node dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM workloads, InfraRSI achieves a speedup of up to $2.75\times$ and lifts mean Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) from $17.4\%$ to $30.0\%$, outperforming existing tuners and coding agents while transferring experience across GPUs. As it improves training infrastructure efficiency, InfraRSI forms a two-level Recursive Self-Improvement loop---revising priors online within runs and distilling experience across clusters---to push foundation model scaling.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管递归自我改进（RSI）加速了孤立算法与内核的合成，但分布式LLM训练依赖于紧密耦合的启动设置、算子内核和通信调度，单次修改常触及内存溢出（OOM）边界、编译器冲突、测量抖动或静默数值漂移。我们提出InfraRSI，这一智能体框架通过五阶段工作流将开放式人类命令转化为经验证的训练优化：init锁定可编辑范围，并针对工作负载、损失和计时不变量固定任务契约以防止奖励黑客；doctor分析基线各阶段并校准集群噪声；run在重新对照基线验证最佳候选并将发现记录到跨硬件经验库之前，协同优化启动旋钮与代码补丁；report和apply审计源路径、跟踪失败试验成本并提交晋升的修改。InfraRSI并非从单一当前最优配置贪心推进，而是从多样化的经验种子配置初始化，并对所有试验（包括OOM）拟合全局执行时间模型和删失峰值内存模型。利用这些模型，它为每个设置的内存成本定价，根据实时运行修正校准不当的LLM先验，并将内存密集型优化与内存节省措施及经验证的代码补丁配对。在四个单节点和多节点稠密与混合专家（MoE）LLM工作负载上，InfraRSI实现最高$2.75\times$的加速，并将平均模型FLOPs利用率（MFU）从$17.4\%$提升至$30.0\%$，优于现有调优器和编码智能体，同时实现跨GPU的经验迁移。在提升训练基础设施效率的同时，InfraRSI形成两级递归自我改进循环——在运行内在线修正先验，并跨集群蒸馏经验——以推动基础模型扩展。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出InfraRSI智能体框架，通过五阶段工作流与全局执行时间/峰值内存建模优化分布式LLM训练，在四个工作负载上实现最高2.75倍加速并将平均MFU从17.4%提升至30.0%。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Layer Roles Matter: Mitigating Modality Imbalance in Multimodal Emotion Reasoning via Adaptive Layer Profiling
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Emotion Reasoning (MER) requires perceiving and integrating emotion cues from multiple modalities. Recent advances increasingly leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to enhance reasoning capacity. However, due to the inherent heterogeneity in conveying emotions across modalities, these models often suffer from modality imbalance and confront flawed emotion understanding. In this paper, we conduct an in-depth analysis on MER models and uncover two key empirical insights. (i) In MER, modality imbalance manifests two distinct failure modes: unimodal over-reliance and insufficient cross-modal utilization, which call for different intervention strategies. (ii) MLLM layers exhibit implicit functional hierarchies in multimodal emotion processing, playing separable roles in stabilizing unimodal representations and integrating cross-modal information. Motivated by these observations, we propose a Layer-Aware Modality Rebalancing (LAMR) framework by explicitly aligning intervention strategies with layer roles. Specifically, we first introduce two quantized metrics for adaptive layer role profiling. In each layer, Modality Entropy (ME) measures the dispersion of modality contributions, and Cross-modal Intensity (CMI) captures the strength of cross-modal interactions. Then, we respectively enhance modality equilibrium in stabilization layers and cross-modal propagation in integration layers. Extensive experiments on two comprehensive MER benchmarks demonstrate that LAMR effectively mitigates modality imbalance and improves emotion reasoning across diverse MLLM backbones, without additional training.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态情感推理（MER）需要从多种模态中感知并整合情感线索。近期进展越来越多地利用多模态大语言模型（MLLM）来增强推理能力。然而，由于不同模态在传达情感时存在固有的异质性，这些模型常常遭受模态不平衡问题，并面临有缺陷的情感理解。本文对MER模型进行了深入分析，揭示了两项关键的经验性发现。（i）在MER中，模态不平衡表现为两种不同的失效模式：单模态过度依赖和跨模态利用不足，二者需要不同的干预策略。（ii）MLLM的层在多模态情感处理中表现出隐式的功能层级，在稳定单模态表示和整合跨模态信息方面扮演可分离的角色。受这些观察启发，我们提出了层感知模态再平衡（LAMR）框架，通过显式地将干预策略与层角色对齐。具体而言，我们首先引入两个量化指标用于自适应层角色刻画。在每一层中，模态熵（ME）衡量模态贡献的分散程度，跨模态强度（CMI）捕捉跨模态交互的强度。然后，我们分别在稳定层增强模态均衡、在整合层增强跨模态传播。在两个综合MER基准上的大量实验表明，LAMR有效缓解了模态不平衡，并在多种MLLM骨干上提升了情感推理，且无需额外训练。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文分析发现MER中模态不平衡表现为单模态过度依赖与跨模态利用不足两种失效模式、且MLLM各层承担稳定单模态表示与整合跨模态信息的不同角色，据此提出无需额外训练的LAMR框架，用模态熵与跨模态强度指标刻画层角色并分层施加干预，在两个MER基准上缓解了模态不平衡并提升情感推理。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Verify Before You Fetch: Reliable KV Cache Compression for LLM Inference
papers.abstract_en: Long-context applications, long-lived agents, and multi-agent systems require large language models (LLMs) to process and retain extensive information. In these settings, the KV cache can exceed GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity, necessitating offloading to host memory, where CPU-to-GPU transfers can dominate inference latency. While KV cache compression can reduce data movement, query-agnostic compression that guarantees accurate attention for arbitrary queries is extremely challenging, if not impossible. We introduce VerKV, a hybrid approach that provides $(ε, δ)$ guarantees for approximating attention on any given query. VerKV maintains a compact set of query-agnostic pivotal tokens on the GPU, together with a token-level sketch of the full KV cache, while retaining the complete cache in CPU memory. We introduce a novel stochastic sampling procedure, PoissonComp, to select the pivotal tokens. At inference time, our proposed KVFetch algorithm uses the pivotal tokens and the sketch to estimate the relative error of the resulting attention computation. If the estimate satisfies a user-specified $(ε, δ)$ tolerance, inference proceeds without accessing host memory. Otherwise, VerKV performs query-aware retrieval to fetch additional tokens from the CPU, refining the attention computation to meet the required tolerance. Thus, VerKV enables attention with bounded approximation error while minimizing CPU-to-GPU transfers. We show that PoissonComp outperforms state-of-the-art approaches to KV cache compression. Combined with KVFetch, it achieves near-dense performance (90-100% of dense quality at 32K context length, averaged over RULER and LOFT), using Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Ministral-3-8B, while reducing the GPU memory footprint by 8-32x and keeping CPU-to-GPU memory fetches within 2-23% of the cache per generated token, depending on the model.
papers.abstract_zh: 长上下文应用、长期存活的智能体和多智能体系统要求大语言模型（LLM）处理并保留大量信息。在这些场景中，KV缓存可能超出GPU高带宽内存（HBM）容量，从而需要卸载到主机内存，而CPU到GPU的传输可能主导推理延迟。虽然KV缓存压缩可以减少数据移动，但保证任意查询下注意力计算准确的查询无关压缩极具挑战，甚至不可能。我们提出VerKV，一种混合方法，对任意给定查询的注意力近似提供$(ε, δ)$保证。VerKV在GPU上维护一组紧凑的查询无关关键令牌（pivotal tokens）以及完整KV缓存的令牌级草图（sketch），同时在CPU内存中保留完整缓存。我们引入一种新的随机采样过程PoissonComp来选择关键令牌。在推理时，我们提出的KVFetch算法利用关键令牌和草图估计所得注意力计算的相对误差。若估计满足用户指定的$(ε, δ)$容差，则推理无需访问主机内存；否则，VerKV执行查询感知检索，从CPU获取额外令牌，细化注意力计算以满足所需容差。因此，VerKV在最小化CPU到GPU传输的同时，实现具有有界近似误差的注意力计算。我们表明PoissonComp优于最先进的KV缓存压缩方法。结合KVFetch，在使用Qwen3-4B、Qwen3.5-9B和Ministral-3-8B时，于32K上下文长度下（在RULER和LOFT上平均）达到接近稠密的性能（稠密质量的90-100%），同时将GPU内存占用降低8-32倍，并将每生成一个令牌的CPU到GPU内存获取量控制在缓存的2-23%以内（取决于模型）。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文提出VerKV混合KV缓存压缩方法：用PoissonComp在GPU上选取查询无关关键令牌并维护全缓存草图、完整缓存在CPU，推理时由KVFetch估计注意力相对误差，满足$(ε, δ)$容差则无需访问主机内存，否则查询感知地取回额外令牌，在32K上下文下达到稠密性能的90-100%并将GPU内存占用降低8-32倍。

limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Hybrid Source Code Change Impact Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Change impact analysis (CIA) helps developers identify code entities impacted by their initial changes. While several approaches for CIA were proposed, they still struggle with either low precision or low recall, thereby increasing manual effort for developers to verify the results. Furthermore, limitations in the used datasets and experimental setups can bias the results reported by many CIA approaches. In this paper, we first address the dataset limitations by manually labeling 1,931 changed code entities stemming from 263 commits of 22 open-source Java projects. Next, we introduce two variants of katIA, our code change impact analysis approach that combines static impact analysis with the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). The first variant uses a single prompt (katIA-SP) for refining an initial static impact set while the second variant uses three specialized agents (katIA-MA). The evaluation with our curated dataset shows that katIA-SP with Gemini 2.5 Flash achieved an F1-score of 22.4% when matching impacted entities by their fully qualified names (FQN) and 27.0% when matching them by their class and entity names (CE). The latter shows an improvement of 2.0 percentage points over the state-of-the-art. This score is further improved by katIA-MA which, using Gemini 2.5 Flash, yields an FQN-matching F1-score of 29.1% and a CE-matching F1-score of 33.3%. While these improvements come at the cost of increased median generation time from 0.570 s to 11.214 s and median token usage from 1,235 to 6,462 tokens, the improved performance justifies the additional cost. The comparison of three LLMs using katIA-SP finds that Gemini 2.5 Flash is the most consistent model. These results indicate that combining static impact analysis with LLM-based refinement, particularly with the multi-agent variant, can improve code change impact analysis.
papers.abstract_zh: 变更影响分析（CIA）帮助开发者识别受其初始变更影响的代码实体。尽管已提出多种CIA方法，它们仍受困于低精确率或低召回率，从而增加开发者验证结果的人工负担。此外，所用数据集和实验设置的局限可能使许多CIA方法报告的结果存在偏差。本文首先通过人工标注来自22个开源Java项目263次提交的1,931个变更代码实体，解决数据集局限问题。接着，我们介绍katIA的两个变体，这是我们结合静态影响分析与大语言模型（LLM）推理能力的代码变更影响分析方法。第一个变体使用单一提示（katIA-SP）来精化初始静态影响集，第二个变体使用三个专门智能体（katIA-MA）。在我们构建的数据集上的评估显示，使用Gemini 2.5 Flash的katIA-SP在按全限定名（FQN）匹配受影响实体时F1分数为22.4%，按类名与实体名（CE）匹配时为27.0%。后者较最先进方法提升2.0个百分点。katIA-MA进一步提升了该分数：使用Gemini 2.5 Flash时，FQN匹配F1分数为29.1%，CE匹配F1分数为33.3%。虽然这些提升以中位生成时间从0.570秒增至11.214秒、中位令牌用量从1,235增至6,462为代价，但性能提升证明了额外成本的合理性。使用katIA-SP对三个LLM的比较发现Gemini 2.5 Flash是最一致的模型。这些结果表明，将静态影响分析与基于LLM的精化相结合，尤其是多智能体变体，可以改进代码变更影响分析。
papers.tldr_zh: 该文人工标注22个Java项目263次提交中的1,931个变更代码实体以构建数据集，并提出结合静态影响分析与LLM精化的katIA：单提示变体katIA-SP在CE匹配下F1为27.0%（较最先进提升2.0个百分点），三智能体变体katIA-MA进一步提升至FQN 29.1%、CE 33.3%，代价是生成时间与令牌用量增加。

papers.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
papers.abstract_en: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE
papers.abstract_zh: 可泛化的深度伪造视频检测仍具挑战性，因为伪造痕迹在不同操纵类型间差异显著，且常混合多样的空间与时间不一致性。现有参数高效适配方法通常依赖单一共享表示，使其易受特定操纵偏差影响，并限制了对未见伪造的迁移能力。为应对这一挑战，我们提出时空专家混合（MoSTE），一种实现取证表示条件化专门化的适配框架。MoSTE不强制单个适配器建模所有伪造模式，而是将适配分解为并行的空间与时间专家池，并通过无监督的令牌级路由机制将令牌动态路由到最相关的专家。这使专家无需显式操纵标签或多阶段训练即可自然专门化于互补的伪造线索，同时有效地将表示从CLIP迁移到视频领域。跨数据集和跨操纵基准的大量实验表明，MoSTE在平均泛化性上树立了新的最先进水平，同时在多种操纵类别上保持强劲性能。对专家路由和注意力行为的额外分析揭示了专家多样性的涌现，表明MoSTE学到了互补的时空取证特征。代码见https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE。

papers.title: MNN-Pocket-0.3B Technical Report
papers.abstract_en: This technical report presents MNN-Pocket-0.3B, a compact 300M-parameter dense language model designed for efficient on-device deployment and supporting context lengths of up to 32K tokens. With an INT4 deployment footprint of only 173 MB and decoding throughput of up to 466 tokens/s on iPad Pro M5 (Metal), it can be seamlessly integrated into applications on edge devices such as smartphones and smart glasses. MNN-Pocket-0.3B is developed through the co-design of its architecture, data, training pipeline, and inference system. Hardware-aware architecture selection and dependency-aware vocabulary pruning balance model capability with on-device memory and compute constraints. A four-stage pre-training pipeline covering approximately 4.1 trillion high-quality Chinese and English tokens equips the model with broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. This is followed by a three-stage post-training pipeline comprising instruction fine-tuning, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and quantization-aware training. Finally, hardware-specific optimizations in the MNN inference engine enable fast, memory-efficient inference and long-context processing. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that MNN-Pocket-0.3B achieves frontier-level performance among models of comparable size, with particularly strong results in Chinese and English knowledge and reasoning, mathematics, coding, and instruction following. It consistently outperforms similarly sized open-source models and even surpasses several 0.5B-parameter models on instruction-following benchmarks. We release MNN-Pocket-0.3B with open weights and ready-to-use MNN deployment packages. We hope it will provide a practical foundation for capable, responsive, and memory-efficient edge applications while advancing research and development in on-device language models.
papers.abstract_zh: 本技术报告介绍MNN-Pocket-0.3B，一个紧凑的3亿参数稠密语言模型，面向高效端侧部署设计，支持最长32K令牌的上下文长度。其INT4部署占用仅173 MB，在iPad Pro M5（Metal）上解码吞吐最高达466令牌/秒，可无缝集成到智能手机和智能眼镜等边缘设备上的应用中。MNN-Pocket-0.3B通过架构、数据、训练流程和推理系统的协同设计开发而成。硬件感知的架构选择与依赖感知的词表剪枝在模型能力与端侧内存和计算约束之间取得平衡。覆盖约4.1万亿高质量中英文令牌的四阶段预训练流程赋予模型广泛的知识与推理能力。随后是三阶段后训练流程，包括指令微调、多教师同策略蒸馏和量化感知训练。最后，MNN推理引擎中针对硬件的优化实现快速、内存高效的推理与长上下文处理。大量评估表明，MNN-Pocket-0.3B在同等规模模型中达到前沿水平，在中英文知识与推理、数学、编程和指令遵循方面表现尤为突出。它持续优于同等规模的开源模型，甚至在指令遵循基准上超过若干0.5B参数模型。我们以开放权重和即用型MNN部署包发布MNN-Pocket-0.3B，希望为能力强、响应快、内存高效的边缘应用提供实用基础，并推动端侧语言模型的研究与开发。

papers.title: BlenderFORGE: Framework for Optimizing Reactive 3D-Graphics Editing Ability of MLLMs
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promise as interactive agents, yet precise, programmatic 3D graphics editing remains difficult to train because existing systems largely rely on closed-source model APIs and lack deterministic, state-verifiable execution environments. We present BlenderFORGE, a trainable data-environment-optimization framework for open-weight MLLM agents that edit explicit Blender scenes through Blender Python (bpy) code generation. BlenderFORGE targets four fundamental state-verifiable editing task families: object placement, shape-key editing, lighting adjustment, and material modification. It integrates three components: (1) a scalable perturbation-based data generation pipeline built from curated assets and large-scale 3D scene repositories; (2) an isolated Blender Sandbox for deterministic code execution, structured state export, and closed-loop reward computation; and (3) a two-stage training pipeline that uses offline teacher trajectories for cold-start Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and sandbox-computed rewards for multi-turn tool-agentic Reinforcement Learning (AgentLoop-RL). Experiments across the four task families show that the resulting open-weight Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B BlenderFORGE agents substantially improve over their base models and achieve competitive performance with several zero-shot proprietary MLLM baselines on selected metrics. Additional cross-benchmark evaluations and camera-reframing experiments provide evidence of transfer beyond the original training setting.

papers.title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
papers.abstract_en: As large language models become more capable agents, they can exhibit deceptive behaviors, cheating human for higher rewards while appearing helpful. We attribute this failure to evaluation-side partial observability, where models are evaluated mainly from final outcome, without checking the faithfulness of underlying reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects. Prior mitigations address this partial observability by predefined evaluator latent belief space or one-shot monitoring, which do not extend to free-form language space and vulnerable to stronger deceptions that evade simple monitoring. In this work, we formulate deception mitigation as an Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Extensive Form Game (e-PoG), a max-min framework in which an agent maximizes reward, a monitor minimizes the agent's payoff by exposing deception from the full interaction trajectory, and a fixed verifier validates the monitor's claims and converts them into penalties. We define the solution concept as a Subgame-Perfect Oversight Equilibrium (SPOE) between agent and monitor, and prove its existence in finite games. With a perfect verifier, every SPOE is faithful; with an imperfect verifier, the guarantee persists if verifier errors do not reverse the ranking of monitor actions. To achieve faithful SPOE, we derive a two-timescale policy gradient algorithm and enhance the pipeline empirically with NLI verification and deterministic checks. Experiments with Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop show that e-PoG mitigates multiple emergent deception modes, outperforming the strongest baselines by 26.0% in deception mitigation and by up to 39.8% in task success. These gains persist under weak-to-strong supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/Toyoid/deceptive-agent.

papers.title: When Credit Turns Against Tools: Transition-Aware Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Agentic reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards trains language models through multi-turn tool interactions, yet their reasoning performance and tool-calling ability can decline during training. We trace this degradation to three coupled mechanisms: (1) tool-token imbalance produces negative overall tool credit when incorrect trajectories contain more tool tokens per turn than correct ones; (2) aggregation amplification can further strengthen this negative signal as token-mean aggregation gives longer incorrect trajectories greater weight in policy updates; and (3) failure-driven retries prolong trajectories as models tend to call tools again after execution errors, extending potential negative credit to recovery attempts. To counter this suppression, we propose Transition-Aware Credit Assignment (TACA), which targets the transition from reasoning to tool use through supervision of both call initiation and generation. Specifically, TACA uses Advantage Projection to enforce a nonnegative mean advantage on tool-call tokens within each prompt group through a minimal uniform shift. Additionally, TACA guides tool-use decisions with Decision Contrast, comparing rewards for tool-assisted and direct answers to the same prompt. Through Supervised Replay, it reinforces tool-call generation using calls from previously sampled correct trajectories. Across models and tasks, TACA improves performance and sustains more reliable tool interaction during training, raising mean accuracy over MT-GRPO on six reasoning benchmarks by 4.61 percentage points for Qwen2.5-1.5B and 3.61 for Qwen2.5-3B. Our code is available at https://github.com/tmlr-group/TACA.

papers.title: Not All Layers Are Equal in Image-to-Video Transfer
papers.abstract_en: Parameter-efficient image-to-video transfer adapts frozen image foundation models to video via lightweight trainable adapters. Existing methods insert the same adapter at every transformer layer, implicitly assuming all layers require equal temporal modeling. A layer-wise sensitivity analysis across four video-native model families and two pretraining paradigms reveals that this assumption is wrong: temporal sensitivity increases with depth, and the pretraining paradigm determines its growth profile. Vision-only models exhibit a gradual rise, while vision-language models show early suppression followed by late recovery. This finding motivates STRAP, a training-free adapter placement rule that derives a spatial-to-temporal transition boundary from a paradigm-matched video model. Spatial adapters are assigned before this boundary and temporal adapters after it, without modifying the adapter architecture itself. On four fine-grained action recognition benchmarks, STRAP improves accuracy by up to 11.8% over uniform placement, reduces trainable parameters by 29 to 48%, and lowers inference time by up to 10%. On standard benchmarks, it matches accuracy with fewer parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/th-nesh/STRAP.

papers.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) offer complementary routes to post-training. For visual agents, however, tool use presents two related challenges. Models may overlook useful tool-returned observations, while poorly grounded actions can limit the evidence available for subsequent distillation. We introduce Reframe, a post-training framework that treats the observation state, rather than only the output distribution, as an object of alignment. First, Ground-Drop-GRPO (GD-GRPO) trains spatial and temporal specialists with evidence-aware rewards and stochastic removal of the original visual input, encouraging them to acquire grounded evidence and use the returned observations. Second, Observation-Gated-MOPD (OG-MOPD) replaces deficient tool actions with canonical ones mid-rollout and resumes distillation from the repaired observation. The two stages complement each other, as learning to rely on tool-returned observations can help the policy benefit from observation repair. Neither stage requires a task-specific SFT cold start. Extensive experiments over 14 image and video benchmarks demonstrate that Reframe outperforms both Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD. Ablation results show that GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain compared with outcome-based GRPO.

papers.title: Viscot-steer: Disentangling and Transferring Visual Chain-of-Thought via Activation Steering
papers.abstract_en: Visual chain-of-thought (visual-CoT), also known as "thinking with images", equips LVLMs with the ability to locate and use key visual evidence for reasoning. However, acquiring such visual-CoT capabilities requires costly post-training and tightly couples them to a specific backbone, making transfer to other LVLMs difficult. Existing cross-model transfer methods typically treat visual-CoT as a monolithic capability, using a unified representation that ignores the functional distinction between grounding and reasoning and introduces stage-irrelevant interventions. To address this problem, we propose Viscot-steer, a training-free activation steering framework for transferring visual-CoT capabilities across heterogeneous LVLMs. Specifically, Viscot-steer first disentangles visual-CoT into grounding and reasoning vectors and extracts them from the source-model layers associated with the corresponding capabilities. It then aligns the vectors with the activation space of the target model and steers the grounding and reasoning layers during bounding-box prediction and reasoning-trace generation, respectively. Across benchmarks covering high-resolution visual understanding, general visual perception and reasoning, and mathematical visual reasoning, Viscot-steer transfers capabilities from different visual-CoT models to architecturally diverse LVLMs and outperforms the strongest capability-transfer baseline by an average of 1.86 percentage points on the primary evaluation metrics.

papers.title: Simple Test-Time Refinement for Plot-to-Code Generation via Visual-Code Diagnostics
papers.abstract_en: Plot-to-code generation has been greatly advanced by recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing studies mainly focus on one-pass generation or iterative sampling guided by verifier-based filtering, which does not align with the typical human programming workflow of generate first, then iteratively error-location and fix. This naturally motivates a test-time refinement paradigm for plot-to-code generation. In this work, we present the first study on plot-to-code generation via iterative test-time refinement. We propose a Visual-Code Diagnostics framework that enables refinement through visual feedback from source code. Specifically, we first categorize generation errors into four coarse-grained types, and then train lightweight discriminators to recognize and localize these errors based on the rendered visual outputs and corresponding code. Unlike traditional compiler- or debugger-based verification, our approach performs iterative refinement guided by one diagnostics system, enabling more effective semantic and visual correction during test time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently improves generation quality across diverse generators and significantly outperforms strong test-time scaling baselines.

papers.title: No Second Run: Does RSI Stop at Frontier Pre-training?
papers.abstract_en: Pre-training is where every foundation model begins; bringing recursive self-improvement (RSI) there would let AI improve the process that creates AI. Yet public RSI work has so far targeted only post-training, which starts from an existing base model, runs trials costing GPU-hours, and returns verifiable scores. Pre-training breaks all three conditions at orders-of-magnitude higher cost: a run consumes hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours over months and cannot be repeated; its objective, post-training headroom, cannot be read off any single score; and what must improve is not a model but the whole production system, from data pipelines and training infrastructure to the teams that run them. To our knowledge, we are the first to apply RSI to an entire frontier pre-training run from scratch and to report it in detail. RSI does not stop at frontier pre-training, but it changes form: since no end-to-end loop can close over a single unrepeatable run, we decompose it into smaller loops that can, each repairing a step the full run breaks. The result is 801-30B-A3B-Base, a 30B-A3B MoE trained from scratch on 11.8T tokens in three months by a newly formed team. We release it as a base model; the lightweight SFT reported here (6B tokens, no RL) only probes post-training headroom. As a base model, 801-30B-A3B outperforms Qwen3-30B-A3B and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B, trailing only the larger Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, and keeps this position under identical SFT; with lightweight SFT alone, it achieves the highest average on four agentic benchmarks against fully post-trained models, including Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Since post-training RSI presupposes a strong base model, bringing RSI into pre-training acts on the foundation every later stage builds on. We open-source 801-30B-A3B-Base and the lightweight SFT data at https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/801-30B .

papers.title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Post-LayerNorm Transformers have seen limited practical adoption due to enduring difficulties in scaling them to large depths. While prior research has focused on stabilising Post-LayerNorm by improving conditioning at initialisation, stability often deteriorates when models are trained with large learning rates, forcing additional compromises. In the decoder-only settings we study, existing Post-LayerNorm methods fail to outperform strong Pre-LayerNorm baselines. We propose KiteNorm, a post-norm training method designed to break this trend by constraining hidden-state variance. This approach is motivated by a bound on the LayerNorm Jacobian suggesting that variance growth contributes to gradient vanishing, alongside empirical evidence linking it to rank collapse. KiteNorm combines residual scaling and variance regularisation to maintain stability throughout training, supported by scalarised double-normalisation that provides separately learnable scales for the skip and residual branches. Across decoder-only Transformers up to 1.3B parameters, KiteNorm improves training stability and outperforms leading baselines at their optimal learning rates, with scaling laws favouring KiteNorm across depth, width, batch size, and training budget. Ablations show that each component is necessary for the full stability and performance gains.

papers.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control
papers.abstract_en: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. SPARK is built on two principles: temporal abstraction, which encourages the encoder to derive compact features that preserve information essential for understanding temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure, and knowledge preservation, which aligns patch-level representations with those of the original foundation model to retain useful pretrained semantics. These objectives yield compact visual state representations that remain semantically meaningful while preserving useful prior knowledge. Experiments across multiple robotics benchmarks show that SPARK consistently improves success rates and generalization over vanilla foundation models, and further demonstrate that these gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation.

papers.title: Direct GPU Energy Measurements of Batch-Level Sharing in Mixture-of-Experts and Recurrent Models
papers.abstract_en: Energy claims for efficient neural networks are often inferred from operation counts. We report direct GPU energy measurements on two workloads that batch very differently, recurrent policies in GPU-vectorised multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models, and ask one question of both: can the rows of a batch be made to share computation, across the batch and over time, at a measured saving? On recurrent policies the answer so far is no. Shared activity patterns exist but rarely last one step, masking a frozen policy fails, and trained-in masks succeed only because a fixed mask is equivalent to a narrow GRU, at 11x the energy of a small dense policy in our implementation. Test-time steering adds nothing beyond re-picking on either workload. On MoE models the answer is yes, and granularity decides how much: on Qwen3-30B-A3B, batch-aware routing reads 25-31% fewer expert weights within KL 0.05, with benchmark changes within noise at 500 items, and uses 12-18% less energy per token on a fused forward. We also introduce persistence-aware OEA, a one-parameter rule that keeps the batch-aware cut with about 40% fewer new experts per step than native routing at batch 32-64, though its energy has not yet been measured. These are pilot measurements on one GPU type, and we state their limits.

papers.title: Deterministic Narrative Gravity: Bridging Theory of Mind and Historical Simulation through ABM-LLM Architectures
papers.abstract_en: Historical social simulation faces a fundamental reproducibility challenge: the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) introduces a digital butterfly effect that prevents exact replication across multi-turn runs. Furthermore, the inability to control low-level server parameters in commercial LLM hosting environments severely limits reproducibility. To overcome this opacity, we present a deterministic multi-agent framework coupling LLMs to an Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) pipeline grounded in Theory of Mind (ToM) and Cognitive Archaeology, and validate exact artifact identity within local, pinned execution environments using SHA-256 hashing. Run locally at temperature zero with clean per-call model reloads, the system injects differentiated cognitive states per turn through dissonance-driven behavioural modes and gated internal voices. Evaluating seven model configurations spanning 4B to 31B parameters against an ablated baseline reveals clear operational boundaries. Small models ($\leq$8B) suffer from context capacity overload, producing repetitive, specular dialogue loops. However, at $\geq$12B parameters, the ABM scaffolding breaks the monotonous response patterns seen in ablation. Crucially, these scaffolded models exhibit spontaneous diegetic expansion: they coherently expand scenario lore through tactically motivated, anachronism-free details rather than escalating into aggression. By resisting the structural pull toward premature scene closure, scaffolded sessions sustain an open terminal Narrative Vector ($V_N = \mathrm{Open}$ in 12/21 overall; 9/9 in official $\geq$12B configurations) whereas unscaffolded ablation never does (0/21). This framework provides a transparent, auditable benchmark architecture for virtual archaeology, with the full pipeline released as open-source software to enable independent replication.

papers.title: Perception, Not Reasoning, Limits Visual Theory of Mind
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. The consensus diagnosis is conceptual, prescribing new belief-reasoning modules. We argue the dominant bottleneck is perceptual: not what the model cannot reason about, but what it cannot see. We propose a five-condition dissociation protocol that holds the reasoning task constant while varying perceptual fidelity from visual only to text only, and quantify the result with the Perceptual Contribution Ratio, the share of the visual-to-text gap a given fidelity closes. We test this on two kinds of scenes: abstract 2D panels in the Heider--Simmel tradition, and naturalistic 3D game scenes from MuMA-ToM and MindPower. The evaluation covers seven VLMs and roughly 159,000 API calls. Ground-truth scaffolds substantially close the gap in every setting, and on the abstract panels and MuMA-ToM they match or exceed the text-only reasoning. Whereas scaffolds built by automatic parsers, including frontier VLMs, fail. The most common error in the visual-only condition is \emph{reality bias}, which accounts for 60\% of false-belief failures. Models report where an object actually is, not where an absent agent believes it is. This points to a perceptual front-end that fails to track which agents were present at each moment. Under the evaluated protocol, structured visual scene-state extraction, rather than belief inference, is the dominant bottleneck for visual ToM.

papers.title: Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Knowledge distillation trains a student language model to match a teacher's predictions on the training text. We ask whether learning the teacher's behavior beyond the training text can further improve the student. We investigate this using three input perturbations: additive token noise, blending two documents, and blending neighboring tokens. Specifically, for an early part of pretraining we perturb the inputs and train the student to match the teacher on them, and we spend the rest of the same token budget on ordinary distillation. When pretraining from scratch, the best method improves on standard distillation at both scales we tried, by 0.025 nats at 135M parameters and by 0.020 nats at 0.5B (mean of three seeds). At 135M this is 1.45 times the gain that distillation itself provides over next-token training. We also observe promising downstream transfer: at 0.5B, the best variant improves average zero-shot accuracy by about one percentage point across seven tasks. It also retains its validation-loss advantage after low-bit weight quantization. We also test a data-limited setting in which training data must be reused, and find that the gains persist. Finally, ablations suggest that, for additive noise, perturbing the teacher's inputs contributes most of the gain, while perturbing only the student's inputs yields much less.

papers.title: OptiCover: A Scalable and Multi-Surface Framework for Cold-Start Visual Optimization under Semantic Constraints
papers.abstract_en: Selecting an effective cover photo is a critical yet understudied problem in visual merchandising for e-commerce marketplaces. On Airbnb, hosts upload many photos depicting different rooms, amenities, and points of interest, but must manually choose a single static cover photo that is reused across heterogeneous product surfaces. This creates substantial challenges: over 90\% of listing photos have no engagement labels, leading to a severe cold-start regime; guest preferences vary across surfaces and search intents, and visually captivating photos may be semantically misaligned with the underlying listing. At Airbnb scale, this corresponds to hundreds of millions of photos and hundreds of thousands of new uploads per day. We propose \emph{OptiCover}, a scalable framework for cold-start visual optimization under semantic constraints and multi-surface engagement signals. The framework combines (i) a photo candidate generator that identifies candidate photos through various proxies, (ii) lightweight vision heads applied to frozen CLIP embeddings for large-scale semantic scoring, (iii) a cross-modal grounding validator based on a vision-language model (VLM) that enforces semantic representativeness, and (iv) an Exploration Logging Module (ELM) that orchestrates the collection of randomized engagement data across heterogeneous product surfaces and contextual search intents. We evaluate OptiCover through extensive offline studies and multiple online experiments across HomePage, and Search surfaces. OptiCover is now deployed in production and performs tens of millions of photo swaps daily. Online results show a 1.5\% engagement lift on the HomePage and a 0.35\% increase in bookers on Search, generating millions of dollars in incremental revenue. Our findings suggest that action-space shaping and semantic constraints are primary drivers of performance.

papers.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
papers.abstract_en: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

papers.title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.

papers.title: A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone
papers.abstract_en: Transformers are built with continuous symmetries in the attention mechanism. We derive $ρ$, a scalar invariant that measures each head's capacity to couple to rotary positional encodings. This framework allows us to analyze heads without forward passes, opening a new research direction into data-independent analysis of modern LLMs. Empirically, we find that $ρ$ predicts induction heads, the most-studied circuit type in mechanistic interpretability, with Spearman correlation between $-0.55$ and $-0.74$ across four bias-free RoPE models spanning $135$M to $7$B parameters. As a preliminary proof of concept, we use $ρ$ to apply YaRN to only the top-50% positional heads, which degrades perplexity less than uniform application. Code is available at https://github.com/MPedraBento/rho-invariant.

papers.title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather
papers.abstract_en: Urban traffic flow prediction is a cornerstone of intelligent transportation systems, yet accurate forecasting under adverse weather conditions remains a significant challenge. Existing data-driven models, while effective for routine patterns, often struggle with the sparse data and complex non-linear shifts associated with rare meteorological events. These methods typically treat environmental contexts as shallow numerical features, failing to capture the underlying semantic reasoning-why and how specific adverse conditions alter mobility behaviors across regions with different functional compositions. To address this limitation, we propose Multi-STG, a unified framework that integrates Large Language Model (LLM)-derived semantic priors with graph-based spatiotemporal learning. Multi-STG introduces an LLM-empowered semantic enhancement module that transforms comprehensive context descriptions such as weather, POIs, and holidays into high-level semantic embeddings, effectively providing a knowledge-driven complement to data scarcity. Furthermore, we design a multimodal attentional fusion mechanism to dynamically weigh heterogeneous inputs and a semantic-enhanced prediction head with gated residual calibration to robustly adjust forecasts based on semantic guidance. Extensive experiments on real-world multi-city private car datasets demonstrate that Multi-STG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing MAE by 11.82\% on average relative to the strongest baseline across three cities, while maintaining stable performance under sparse and non-stationary conditions.

papers.title: From Game Generation to Game Playing: Fully Automated Ability Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract_en: Training vision-language-action (VLA) models to follow gameplay instructions across diverse games is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. We introduce a framework that automatically generates game environments and expert demonstrations. An LLM-powered agent uses game-building tools to construct executable environments and tasks targeting specified skills. Programmatic experts then use privileged simulator state to generate aligned instructions, rendered observations, and keyboard and mouse actions. We train our game policy, Script2Play, by post-training a 4B vision-language model with behavior cloning on 150.3 hours of synthetic Minecraft and Roblox gameplay, without human gameplay demonstrations or reinforcement learning. Evaluation on multiple public game benchmarks demonstrates that Script2Play follows gameplay instructions effectively and generalizes across game engines, highlighting the effectiveness of targeted synthetic supervision.

papers.title: Learning Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: LLM-driven time series forecasting has become increasingly promising by leveraging contextual features to generate future values directly or refine forecast priors. However, incorporating contextual features alone does not ensure that models can identify which features matter for forecasting and understand what they suggest about future dynamics. We argue that the fundamental challenge is how to extract predictive evidence from contextual features and when and how to leverage it to guide forecasting decisions. In this paper, we propose CastReasoner, an evidence-grounded reasoning model for context-aware time series forecasting. Specifically, CastReasoner uses a structured chain of thought (CoT) to extract predictive evidence from contextual features, infer the future dynamics suggested by this evidence, and assess these dynamics against the forecast prior to guide adaptive forecasting decisions. To enable this capability, we design a reasoning-centric two-stage post-training framework including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). First, we synthesize reasoning trajectories through controllable multi-teacher guidance and select high-quality ones using a novel student-aware difficulty metric. Second, we design fine-grained multi-objective rewards to further improve reasoning and forecasting. To address heterogeneous learning needs across domains in both stages, we introduce a convergence-guided data balancing strategy. Through this two-stage training, CastReasoner improves both reasoning quality and predictive accuracy. Extensive experiments across multi-domain forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that CastReasoner achieves superior forecasting performance.

papers.title: GenRM-Flow: Generators are Process-aware Reward Models in Flow Matching
papers.abstract_en: Aligning video generation models with human preference depends critically on the quality of the reward model that scores generated videos. Current video reward models, however, source their reward signal from a model's representational rather than generative capacity: they either repurpose vision-language models as pixel-space scorers, or train auxiliary scoring heads on top of frozen generator features. The generator's actual ability to predict velocities, denoise latents, and produce videos plays no role in scoring its own generations. We argue that this overlooks a structural property of offline preference learning. Any preference optimization objective that approximates an offline preference dataset mathematically targets a strictly defined KL-constrained optimal policy. By isolating the reward term from this analytical solution and mapping the exact generation log-likelihood to its flow-matching surrogate, the empirical reward emerges deterministically as the relative difference in continuous-time velocity-prediction errors. We formalize this equivalence into GenRM-Flow, a framework where a preference-tuned video generator inherently operates as a process-aware reward model directly in the noisy latent space. We further show theoretically that distinct fine-tuning objectives, whether contrastive like DPO and IPO or non-contrastive like RWR, are alternative optimization pathways toward the same optimal policy, each inducing a reward readout from the generator's velocity-prediction errors. Furthermore, the extracted process reward seamlessly substitutes external VLM scorers in FlowAWR. Operating purely on native latent outputs without auxiliary reward networks, this generative reward drives measurable improvements in downstream video generation.

papers.title: RoadState: A Domain-Prior-Enhanced Vision-Language System for Industrial-Grade Lane-Level Map Updating
papers.abstract_en: Lane-level map updating requires temporally consistent, physically valid, and auditable road-scene semantics despite occlusions, ambiguous lane markings, temporary obstacles, and viewpoint changes. We present RoadState, a production-deployed vision-language system that transforms sequential road-scene observations into structured lane-level semantics for Baidu Maps' map-updating pipeline. Its core model, RoadState-VLM, formulates road-scene understanding as autoregressive state estimation, predicting the current structured road state from the previous observation and symbolic state together with the current observation. We introduce Geometric Chain-of-Thought (Geo-CoT), which uses a directed acyclic graph of semantic dependencies as a domain prior to improve semantic consistency and reasoning fidelity across interdependent road-state dimensions. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset show that RoadState-VLM achieves 94.33% mean accuracy across six road-state dimensions, outperforming the strongest fine-tuned VLM baseline. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary effectiveness of Geo-CoT and temporal transition context. A cascaded routing pipeline directs routine cases to lightweight models while reserving complex cases for RoadState-VLM. Since its deployment in March 2025, RoadState has supported lane-level map updating across more than 360 cities and reduced overall production costs by 30%. Together with human-in-the-loop auditing, the system maintains robust performance under stress-test conditions. These results demonstrate how domain-prior-enhanced reasoning, structured state interfaces, selective routing, and human quality control can bridge the gap between VLM-based road-scene understanding and large-scale lane-level map updating.

papers.title: SWHForest: A Structural Curation and Search Layer for Large-Scale Code Corpora
papers.abstract_en: Pre-training code language models relies on massive code corpora usually streamed over the internet. However, researchers rarely need a multi-terabyte archive in its entirety; instead, their workflow centers on curated subsets: selecting well-documented files, filtering out repetitive boilerplate, auditing for benchmark contamination, or retrieving specific code patterns. Yet, because modern corpora are typically published as file pointers and basic attributes rather than source text, no general structural layer exists to select which files to download: curating a subset requires downloading and parsing millions of files first just to discard most of them. We present SWHForest, an open-source framework and public dataset that provides this missing structural layer for any pointer-based corpus without redistributing source code. A single pass over the archive parses each file into an AST and immediately discards the source text, keeping only its structural summary. Queried locally or exposed by archive providers as a server-side filtering API, SWHForest selects matching files first (via SQL or index intersection) and downloads only surviving candidates. Across the ten largest languages of Stack-Edu (52.1M unique files, 341M definitions), SWHForest answers curation queries in milliseconds while cutting downloads by 46-72%, reducing live structural searches from hours of per-language streaming to seconds or minutes.

papers.title: When Calibration Data Matter in Sub-4-Bit Language Model Quantization
papers.abstract_en: Low-bit post-training quantization reduces language-model memory but can sharply degrade downstream task accuracy. Calibration usually relies on generic text, but when task-informed data recover accuracy and which quantizers benefit remain poorly understood. We introduce FragCal-DC, which supplements generic text with training documents from task families with low retention of full-precision accuracy in a two-bit scan. We use a two- to four-bit sweep to locate functional regimes and four-seed calibration comparisons to evaluate six data-dependent methods across six dense models (1.7B-8B) and ten tasks. At their lowest tested functional bit widths, iterative SignRound V2 and OmniQuant improve at two bits, whereas single-pass GPTQ and AWQ show small mean responses at three bits. At two bits, SignRound V2 gains 1.83 percentage points in mean ten-task accuracy over generic-text calibration across six models. At 70 billion parameters, GPTQ and SignRound V2 both improve at two bits, with functional generic-calibration baselines. For two-bit SignRound V2, task-level controls show that recovery concentrates on families included in calibration, while incorrect answer designations retain about 90% of the mean accuracy gain. Changes in reconstruction error do not consistently track accuracy gains. These findings support task-informed calibration as a design principle for preserving downstream accuracy in low-bit quantization.

papers.title: AERO: Adaptive Ensemble-Disagreement Routing for Oracle Feedback in Sample-Efficient Online RLHF
papers.abstract_en: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has driven substantial improvements across a wide range of tasks, but the cost of acquiring preference labels remains the dominant bottleneck in the alignment pipeline. While many recent alignment methods improve sample efficiency through active exploration over candidate responses, they typically query the oracle uniformly across contexts, even for contexts where the learned reward estimates are already reliable enough to provide synthetic labels. We propose Adaptive Ensemble-disagreement Routing for Oracle feedback (AERO), a fully online RLHF algorithm built on a Dyna-style model-based RL architecture, in which an ensemble-based Epistemic Reward Model (ERM) serves both as a reward posterior for exploration and as a learned preference-feedback model for synthetic labeling. AERO uses ensemble vote entropy, a Query-by-Committee disagreement measure, combined with an adaptive thresholding mechanism to decide which contexts require oracle feedback and which can instead receive ERM-based synthetic preference labels, concentrating expensive labels where they are most informative. Empirical results across different model families and scales show that AERO achieves highly competitive alignment performance while reducing the required oracle-query budget compared to online DPO and strong active-exploration baselines.
